It's just easier to avoid those activities entirely than to have them see me struggling.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any feelings of detachment from yourself or the world around you, as if you're observing things from outside your body or like you're in a fog?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really felt anything like that. Most of my focus has just been on how stressed and on edge I feel during the day.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned earlier that you don't feel detached, but can you tell me if you've had any experiences where you felt like you were reliving a particularly stressful moment from work, or if you've had any flashbacks to a specific event that's been bothering you?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any flashbacks or felt like I was reliving a specific moment. My struggle is more about the constant, daily stress of the workload and feeling overwhelmed all the time, rather than re-experiencing a single past event.\n\nDoctor: Have you been avoiding talking or thinking about your work situation or any specific aspects of it because it feels too distressing or overwhelming?\n\nPatient: I don't think I'm avoiding thinking or talking about the work situation—honestly, it feels like I can't stop worrying about it. My struggle is more about the constant, daily stress of the workload and feeling overwhelmed all the time, rather than re-experiencing a single past event.\n\nDoctor: Have you been avoiding talking or thinking about your work situation or any specific aspects of it because it feels too distressing or overwhelming?\n\nPatient: I don't think I'm avoiding thinking or talking about the work situation—honestly, it feels like I can't stop worrying about it.
